column2: VP - Learning Experience
column4:
Thanks Yogesh for your feedback. I am the head of learning experience at upGrad. We take learner feedback very strongly - and I did take out time to go through your case. Having trained over 350K learners - we do understand many issues that our learners face. 

AI/ML is a tough field and requires a sufficient amount of learning along with serious practice. For each of our program - content (video content) is recorded by top industry professionals and faculty and is updated every quarter basis feedback from learners and experts. This is 20-30% of learning. A lot of learning is through hands-on practice, projects and live sessions. Feedback for these projects is given using structured rubrics. In case further clarification is required, we connect the learner with industry experts.

Given the rigour, some of the learners do end up not clearing the program - as we are quite strict with the passing criteria.

In such cases, we help our learners in multiple ways, including 1:1 interactions with experts, doubt resolution sessions etc. We offered you the same help. And offering this again here. Please get back to us on this, a lot of good can still happen. Data Science is a beautiful area with great career prospects.

column2: Machine Learning | Deep Learning | NLP | Computer Vision | Lifelong Learner
column4:
Ronnie Screwvala
I have completed the PGDDS program and was part of the October 2017 batch. 
I have the following suggestions that need to be incorporated:
1. Focus on Advanced Content: The course does NOT dive into advanced topics. These include Deep Learning, Natural Language Processing and Computer Vision. These topics are being used predominantly currently in the industry. 
2. Important concepts not paid attention: The course just glosses over core fundamental and essential topics such as Dimensionality Reduction, Feature Engineering and Feature Selection. Despite being a 11 month program, no project/hands-on on an end to end model deployment. We are just given standard csv files where we do our analysis and arrive at results. 
3. Few Topics not explained in depth: Topics like Time Series Forecasting and the module on Big Data Engineering overview were very poorly covered. Despite mass complaints, no action was taken. These topics need to have a serious relook. Also, the course is long enough to have enough time to at least cover some of the mathematical concepts used. These were not present at all.
4. No placement support. Everyone in our batch is very disappointed with the poor placement support.
